description_en: Ibāḥ Bahī is one of the major monasteries of Patan. It is located to the south of Patan Darbar Square and on the right side of the route leading  to Lagankhel. The original name of the Bahī is Rājaśrī Vihāra. In NS 547 (1427 CE) Rājasiṃha Malla, a major Mahāpātra of Lalitpur, reconstructed this Vihāra together with four other Mahāpātras. The Vihāra was previously known as Siṃhavarṇa Mahāvihāra; however, once reconstruction had finished it became known as Rājaśrī due to this connection. Its local name, Ibāḥ, is derived from the Newari word 'ye', which means 'southern direction'. (Śākya2008, 15)This Bahī stands on two raised plinths (measuring 67 cm and 107 cm respectively). It can be accessed by climbing steps that are guarded by two large stone lions on either side. These steps lead up to the door of the main façade, which is to the east. The door is embedded in a decorative doorframe displaying carvings of wisdom bearers and is flanked by two blind windows with images of Bhairava. A projecting balcony juts out above the doorway. This section above the main façade is particularly is impressive; built with traditional timber lathe work, the balcony exhibits features such asdãdikvatā(rod pattern balusters) andphirphircā. Its fascia board is exquisitely carved with images of lotus foliage and scrolls.Entering the colonnaded Phalcā, one can find an image of Mahākāla to the right and Hanumān to the left. The main shrine is located in the west wing, and its central carved door faces east. It can be circumambulated via a narrow passage at the west wall. A single flight of stairs on the southeast corner to the left of the Phalcā leads to the upper floor. There are two exit doors: one on the southeast corner and the other on the right side of the main sanctum (on the western wall) - this leads to a small courtyard called Ibā Dune. The ground floor had no operable windows, but two small openings have been added at the northwestern corner for ventilation. Cross-walls standing perpendicular to the exterior wall divide the ground floor into various small spaces.Outside, the two-tiered plinth is sheltered by the projected balcony. The upper floor also has surrounding balconies that look into the courtyard from all four sides. Its external wall was constructed in brick masonry and contains small lattice windows in all wings. A carved wooden door on the first floor leads to the sanctum room. Each of the building's four wings are covered with tiled roof. They meet each other at the corners, thus forming a valley. Above the shrine, the west wing's roof is surmounted by aphucā(belvedere) with wooden latticework. The roof of thephucāis also covered with tiles, and it has astūpaon a brick base as its pinnacle.The brickwork and type of materials used in each wing vary, suggesting multiple phases of reconstruction and renovation works. The eastern and northern wings were restored between 1990-1993 and the southern and western wings were restored between 1993-1995. The reconstruction work was undertaken by the Nippon Institute of Technology in Japan and the Department of Archaeology in Nepal.A copper plate inscription nailed to the front wall of the shrine is dated NS 547 and states that a golden statue of a Bodhisattva was established in the sanctum of the Bahī. However, the statue was stolen around 1979-80. A new brass statue of the deity was then commisisoned and installed in its place. The entrance of the sanctum is flanked by wall paintings of Maudgalyāyana and Sāriputra and is highly decorated, though it has notoraṇa. Instead, a wooden image of an eight-handed Mahāvairocana holding a sword, an arrow, a hook, andvajrain his right hands and a book, a bow, a noose and a bell in his left has been placed on top of the door. A wall painting of Amoghapāśa Lokeśvara can be found to the left of the door; similarly, one of Mañjuśrī can be found to the right. A bell donated in NS 903 (1783 CE) hangs to the left of the entrance. The north-facing side of the sanctum contains statues of Amoghapāśa Lokeśvara, Dīpaṃkara Buddha, an elephant and some other broken statues.The sunken courtyard (measuring 11.6 m x 11.6 m) further houses a Dharmadhātu Maṇḍala, a statue of donors and an Aśoka Caitya. These are all lined up with the main shrine.Locke(1975, 191) states that this Bahī once owned thirty-eightropanīsof land, which provided a good income. However, he writes that this was lost due to a dispute. Before 1995, a public school called Ādarśa Śikṣā Sadana ran the Bahī-complex for some years. However, the school moved out after the renovation. Today, a college named Sugata Bauddha Vidyālaya is located in the Bahī.
description_ne: मंगलबजारको दक्षिणतिर रहेको चाकबहाल टोलको चौबाटोमा इबा: बही अवस्थित छ । संस्कृतमा यसलाई राजश्री महाविहार भनिन्छ । यस विहारको पुरानो नाम सिंहवर्ण महाविहार थियो, नेसं ५४७ मा ललितपुरका प्रधान महापात्र राजसिंह मल्ल लगायत अन्य चारजना महापात्रहरूले यस विहारको पुनर्निर्माण गरेपछि यसको नाम राजश्री महाविहार नाम रहन गएको हो भन्ने भनाइ छ । स्लसर (1982, plate 157) ले पनि यस विहारलाई 'सिंहवर्ण महाविहार' नै लेखेकी छिन् । नेवारीमा इबा:बहीको अर्थ 'दक्षिण विहार' हो । नेवारीमा दक्षिण दिशालाई 'ये' भनिन्छ, दिशाबोधक 'ये' शब्द ध्वनि परिवर्तन भई 'इ' बनेको हो । मणिगल राजदरबारको दक्षिणतिर रहेका विहारहरूको प्रमुख प्रशासकीय विहार हुनाले यसलाई दक्षिण विहार भनिएको थियो (Śākya 2008, 15) ।यस विहारमा प्रवेश गर्न अग्ला खुड्किलाहरू बनाइएका छन् । खुड्किलामा दायाँ-बायाँ विशाल सिंह राखिएका छन् । विहारको मूल प्रवेशद्वारको माथि बार्दली बनाइएको छ । मूल प्रवेशद्वारबाट भित्र छिरेपछि दक्षिणतिर फल्चा बनाई भित्तामा हनुमान् स्थापना गरिएको छ । मूल प्रवेशद्वारको उत्तर दिशामा एउटा ढुंगा र एउटा काठको गरी दुईवटा महाकालको मूर्ति स्थापना गरिएको छ । मूल प्रवेशद्वारको ठीक सामुन्ने विहारकोद्य:छेँरहेको छ । झिंगटीले छाएकोद्य:छेँको छानामाथि पुर (फुल्चा) राखिएको छ । विहारको गर्भगृहमा पूर्वाभिमुख गरी अक्षोभ्य बुद्ध राखिएको छ । नेसं ५४७ मा विहार निर्माण गरिँदा प्रमुख देवता गन्धुरीभट्टारकको रूपमा सुनको बोधिसत्त्व स्थापना गरिएको भनी ताम्रपत्रमा लेखिए पनि अहिले ढलोटको अक्षोभ्य बुद्धको मूर्ति छ । विसं २०३६-३७ सालतिर सुनको अक्षोभ्य बुद्ध चोरी भएपछि नयाँ ढलोटको मूर्ति बनाएर राखिएको हो । पहिले गन्धकुटी परिक्रमा गर्न प्रदक्षिणापथ बनाइएको थियो (Locke 1975, 189) तर अहिले प्रदक्षिणापथ राखिएको छैन । गन्धकुटीभित्र पस्ने ढोकामा अनेक बुट्टा कोरी कलात्मक बनाइएको छ । ढोकामाथि तोरण राखिएको छैन, तर सिंहलाई आसन बनाएका महावैरोचनको काष्ठमूर्ति राखिएको छ । आठ हात भएका महावैरोचनले दायाँ हातमा खड्ग, वाण, अंकुश र वज्र धारण गरेका छन् भने बायाँ हातमा पुस्तक, धनुष, पाश र घण्टा लिएका छन् । प्रवेशद्वारको दायाँ-बायाँ सारिपत्र र मौदगल्यायनको चित्र कुँदिएको छ । त्यस्तै प्रवेशद्वारको दक्षिणतिर अमोघपाश लोकेश्वर र उत्तरतिर मञ्जुश्रीको चित्र पनि कुँदिएको छ । विहारको गर्भगृहको बाहिर दायाँ-बायाँ सुरक्षार्थ एक जोडी सिंह राखिएको छ । गर्भगृहको दक्षिणतिर नेसं ९०३ मा चढाइएको घण्टा रहेको छ । गर्भगृहसँगै टाँस्सिएर उत्तरतर्फ रहेको खुल्ला ठाउँमा अमोघपाश लोकेश्वर, दीपंकर बुद्ध लगायत हात्ती र केही टुटेफुटेका मूर्तिहरू राखिएका छन् ।विहार परिसरमा एउटा धर्मधातु, दुईजना दाताहरूको मूर्ति र अशोक चैत्य रहेको छ । पश्चिम-दक्षिण कुनामा क्षेत्रपाल रहेको छ । भुइँतल्लामा चारैतिर काठको कलात्मक बार लगाइएको छ भने पहिलो तल्लामा तल झुकेको बरण्डा लगाइएको छ । केही वर्ष पहिले यो विहार निकै जीर्ण अवस्थामा थियो । कुनै समयमा ३८ रोपनी जग्गा सम्पत्ति भएको (Locke 1975: 191) यो विहार आपसी झगडाको कारणले जीर्ण बन्दै गयो । प्राचीन कलाकृतिको धनी रहेको यो विहारबाट थुप्रै कलाकृति र अभिलेखहरू गायब भैसकेका छन् । पहिला यहाँ आदर्श शिक्षा सदन नामको एउटा विद्यालय पनि संचालन गरिएको थियो । विसं २०५२ सालमा विहारको जीर्णोद्धार सम्पन्न भएपछि विद्यालय अन्यत्र सारियो । अहिले विहारमा सुगत बौद्ध विद्यालय नामको कलेज चलाइएको छ ।

monument_assessment: Good (very few light surface damages, renovated or repaired), Repaired

historical_events.event_description: Bhājumāna and Siramāya donated a small bell. This hangs in front of the entrance to the sanctum.

historical_events.event_name: Establishment of gold gilded icon of Bodhisattva
historical_events.event_description: A gilded icon of Bodhisattva was established as a Gandhurī Tathagata in the Vihāra.
Lakṣāhuti Yajña (a one hundred thousand oblation sacrifice) was performed.
A new bell was donated to the main deity of the Vihāra as the old one was damaged. The donors were Jayanarasiṃha, Kitiju, Sidhsiṃju, Basudeva and Ānanda.

A staircase was installed to connect the ground floor to the first floor (second storey). The staircase was constructed by Takṣakāra Mela and its donors were Laṇhasiju and Viśeśvaju from Haḥkha, as well as Halisaṃṣara (Hariśaṃkara) from Tulāchẽ.

Those involved in laying the foundations of the Vihāra were as follows:1. Śrī Dakṣina Vihāra kulumbaja Mahāpātra Rājasiṃha Malla Varmā, who calls himself a devotee of Lokeśvara,2. Pradhāna Mahāpātra Śrī Udayasiṃha Malla Varmā3. Pradhāna Mahāpātra Śrī Jayadharmasiṃha Malla Varmā4. Pradhāna Mahāpātra Śrī Rudrasiṃha Malla Varmā5. Pradhāna Mahāpātra Śrī Jayabhīma Malla Varmā(Vajrācārya2011, 277-278)

A copperplate inscription details the consecration of the monastic building. The Vihāra was consecrated in the presence of King Jayajyotira Malla. An offering of three golden kalaśa was made and a play namedVīrabāhuand written by Rām Bhāro was performed. The chief of Vajrācārya played Śrī Panḍuju of Bubāhā and Karma Vajrācārya was played by Śrī Lokarāmaju from Taḥbāhā. It is written that Jyantarāma Mulmi worked hard to complete the monastic building. This copper plate inscription was made by Udaya Rāut.
The Vihāra was renovated: this saw the brickwork on the external walls of the first and second floor replaced.

historical_events.event_name: Construction of the main entrance of the Vihāra
historical_events.event_description: The main entrance of the Vihāra was erected.

The restoration was completed in two phases. The first phase (1990-1993) saw restoration carried out on sections of the eastern and northern buildings. During this phase, technical assistance was offered by the Agency for Cultural Affairs of Japan, and the cost of restoration was borne jointly by the government of Nepal and the Nippon Institute of Technology. During the second phase (1993-1995) restoration work was carried out on the southern and western buildings. The cost of restoration for the second phase was borne solely by the Nippon Institute of Technology.
